title: Chai-2 Achieves Double-Digit Zero-Shot De Novo Design of Full-Length Therapeutic Antibodies & GPCR Agonists
whyItMatters: First model with double-digit zero-shot hit rates designing full-length IgG antibodies, functional GPCR agonists, and mutation-specific cancer binders from <50 designs instead of million-clone libraries.
summary: Following its June 2025 launch, Chai Discovery published a December 2025 bioRxiv study (10.1101/2025.11.29.691346v2) demonstrating Chai-2’s atomic-precision zero-shot design of full-length monoclonal antibodies (IgGs) against notoriously hard target classes. Evaluating fewer than 50 in silico designs per target without wet-lab library screening, Chai-2 achieved a 100% target hit rate across tested GPCRs (median 24% per-target hit rate), produced the first in silico-designed functional GPCR agonist antibodies, generated low-nanomolar IgGs discriminating single amino-acid cancer mutations on peptide–MHC complexes, and yielded >86% therapeutic-grade developability profiles.
technicalHighlights: Designed full-length IgG antibodies with >86% therapeutic-grade developability and experimental crystal structures matching in silico predictions to atomic accuracy.
Generated validated binders for all tested GPCRs (median 24% hit rate from <50 designs) including the first functional GPCR agonist antibodies designed purely in silico.
Produced low-nanomolar peptide–MHC antibodies selectively distinguishing single-residue tumor neoepitope mutations from wild-type peptides.
caveats: Posted as a company-authored bioRxiv preprint with proprietary model weights; designed antibodies are proof-of-concept preclinical binders rather than clinical drug candidates.

scoreRationale.foundational: Cracked zero-shot de novo design of complex, loop-heavy full-length monoclonal antibodies and functional GPCR agonists without library screening.
scoreRationale.ripple: Signals a structural shift in biologics drug discovery from million-clone empirical screening toward programmable, double-digit-design antibody engineering.
scoreRationale.verification: Backed by extensive wet-lab binding, functional agonist, developability, and experimental structural validation, though proprietary and not yet journal peer-reviewed.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed multi-month million-variant phage/yeast-display campaigns into <50 zero-shot in silico designs.

sources.label: bioRxiv — Drug-like antibody design against challenging targets with atomic precision (Chai-2, Dec 2025)
